To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Mauritian state is a deliberative democratic developmental state that retains the sovereignty of providing contexts for trade making policy that forms the basis of its engagement in the international system.

(1) the state structures are not a mere backdrop but a context in which actors formulate policies, (2) actors are not merely rational but are embedded in the state structures, (3) the actors’ rationality is shaped by the context, and (4) the state structures provide the basis for engagement of the state in the international political and economic system.

(a) The Mauritian State is a deliberative democratic developmental state; (b) The state is an actor in trade making; (c) Trade making is an interactive process that involves a range of actors in the state; (d) The state is a structure that is the context within which actors formulate trade policy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of the existence of the African state in its context of trade policymaking.
the question: how do state structures shape the strategies and actions of political actors as they formulate trade policies in Africa?
the role of states as structures in the formulation of trade policy and the implications of this for the African state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the state in Mauritius is a structure that is a product of a historical and political context that has been shaped and reshaped by political actors in the context that is the Mauritian state.
the Mauritian state has a developmental agenda that is not necessarily a neo-patrimonially driven state.
the African state is a structure that favours certain political actors in the formulation of socio-economic policies and strategies for socio-economic development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the state is a structure in which actors engage to make policies and pursue strategies in order to develop their countries and engage in the international political economic system.
the Mauritian state is a structure that provides a context in which political actors engage in trade policy making.
the state in Africa is not a ‘failed’ state, but rather a state with a ‘failed’ political system that has not adequately addressed the needs of the citizens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the state is a structure and a process that is a product of human interaction and deliberation.
the African state is a structure that is not only the product of the political actors but is also a structure that provides the context for policy-making.
African states have the ability to engage in the international political system as sovereign states and that they can be developmental.
